demos.claim_a: Portfolio rebalancing triggers are evaluated on a fixed quarterly basis.
demos.claim_b: Accounts with a declared risk tolerance below 3 on a 10-point scale trigger a mandatory rebalancing review if any single asset class deviates more than 5% from its target allocation, regardless of the quarterly schedule.
demos.reasoning: Claim A says rebalancing is assessed only on a fixed quarterly basis, while Claim B adds an additional mandatory review trigger that applies immediately when specified deviation and risk-tolerance conditions are met, so the rules can coexist.
demos.extracted_conditions:
Claim A: fixed quarterly basis.
Claim B: declared risk tolerance below 3 on a 10-point scale; any single asset class deviates more than 5% from its target allocation; regardless of the quarterly schedule.
demos.extracted_actions:
Claim A: evaluate rebalancing triggers quarterly.
Claim B: mandate a rebalancing review when the risk-tolerance and deviation conditions are met, even outside the quarterly schedule.

demos.claim_a: Interest on personal loans is compounded monthly.
demos.claim_b: Unless otherwise specified in the executed loan agreement, interest on loans exceeding $500,000 in principal is compounded daily.
demos.reasoning: The claims concern the same subject, loan interest compounding, but apply under different conditions and specify different compounding frequencies, so they do not logically exclude each other.
demos.extracted_conditions: Claim A: personal loans; Claim B: loans exceeding $500,000 in principal, unless otherwise specified in the executed loan agreement
demos.extracted_actions: Claim A: interest is compounded monthly; Claim B: interest is compounded daily

demos.claim_a: Fixed-rate mortgage early repayment penalties apply to any payment exceeding 20% of the outstanding principal in a single calendar year.
demos.claim_b: Borrowers may prepay up to 25% of the original mortgage principal annually without incurring early repayment charges.
demos.reasoning: The two claims set different annual prepayment thresholds for mortgage penalties, so payments between 20% and 25% of principal would be both penalized and penalty-free under the same general context.
demos.extracted_entities: Fixed-rate mortgage early repayment penalties / mortgage prepayments
demos.extracted_conditions: Applied to mortgage payments/prepayments made within a single calendar year, with claim_a using 20% of outstanding principal and claim_b using 25% of original mortgage principal
demos.extracted_actions: Claim_a: impose early repayment penalties on any payment exceeding 20% of outstanding principal in a year; Claim_b: allow annual prepayment up to 25% of original principal without early repayment charges

demos.claim_a: The standard post-discharge follow-up window for Type 2 diabetes patients is 4 weeks.
demos.claim_b: Patients discharged following a hypoglycemic episode that required IV dextrose administration must schedule follow-up within 72 hours of discharge.
demos.reasoning: The claims regulate different follow-up timelines for different patient conditions, and the second does not negate the first because it applies only to a specific hypoglycemic discharge scenario.
demos.extracted_conditions: Claim A: Type 2 diabetes patients after discharge. Claim B: Patients discharged after a hypoglycemic episode requiring IV dextrose.
demos.extracted_actions: Claim A: Follow-up is set at 4 weeks post-discharge. Claim B: Follow-up must be scheduled within 72 hours of discharge.

demos.claim_a: Uncomplicated urinary tract infections in non-pregnant adults are treated with a 3-day course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
demos.claim_b: Standard antibiotic therapy for uncomplicated UTI requires a minimum 7-day treatment course.
demos.reasoning: The claims concern the same condition and treatment type, but they prescribe different mandatory antibiotic durations—3 days versus a minimum of 7 days—so they cannot both hold under the same circumstances.
demos.extracted_entities: Uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI), antibiotic treatment, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
demos.extracted_conditions: Uncomplicated UTI; claim A further limits to non-pregnant adults
demos.extracted_actions: Claim A: treat with a 3-day course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole; Claim B: require a minimum 7-day antibiotic treatment course

signature.instructions:
Evaluate two claims from different enterprise systems. 
Strip away the domain vocabulary and extract the raw entities, conditions, and actions.
Determine if the two actions can logically co-exist under the exact same conditions.

fields.description: The policy or rule stated by System A
The policy or rule stated by System B
A one-sentence explanation of the logical proof.
What is the core subject? (e.g., Metformin, PTO, Server Access)
Under what specific conditions do these rules apply? (e.g., eGFR < 30, Friday afternoons)
What actions are mandated or forbidden by each claim?
Must be exactly one of: 'Contradiction', 'Entailment', or 'Neutral'.
